root_cause_commits_referenced: Source-level fixes for the four Codex requirements landed across 2026-04-28/2026-04-29 commits but never reached the user-visible runtime because (a) experimentalRawEvents was committed as false; (b) shouldRenderToolContent was reverted to hasSpecializedView during the 2026-04-25 scope-leak rollback; (c) MCP elicitation gate was committed with the narrow form+codex_approval_kind condition; (d) the dev daemon at /root/.happy-dev/daemon.state.json predates 4-28/4-29; (e) happy-app:dev image at sha256:33d0b8f6... was created 2026-04-28T13:42 — older than several app sources.
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Source-level changes were correct but not wired through to the user-visible runtime. The four fix groups all required either a flag flip, a whitelist relaxation, an attachment-scope decision, or a daemon/image refresh — and the chain `source -> dist -> daemon -> image -> live UI` was never closed in a single cycle.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: This cycle (a) flips the protocol gate so raw events flow; (b) relaxes the MCP gate so Playwright MCP elicitations are routed through the approval handler instead of cancelled; (c) makes the dev-UI affordance match the actual attachment pipeline; (d) gates the rendering whitelist on Codex-source signal so Codex generic/unknown/resource tools render inline while Claude generic tools stay collapsed; (e) rebuilds the dist for the daemon and the image for the web; (f) leaves the daemon-restart step to the user per spec policy.

codex_consultation.query_verbatim_summary: USER REQUIREMENT: Close the runtime loop on four Codex fixes (MCP elicitation accept; specialized renderers populate; image attachments work; Claude generic tools collapsed AND Codex generic/unknown render inline) so the user verdict 彻底没有实现需求 is invalidated by live dev-UI evidence. Three challenge questions: (1) S5 — safe to treat ALL mcpServer/elicitation/request as approvals? safe response shape? (2) S2 — best signal to distinguish Codex vs Claude tool: name prefix, source discriminant on ToolCall, renderer registry, fixture pattern? (3) Adversarial — concrete reasons this two-line fix could still fail D1/D2/D3/D4 evidence.
codex_consultation.feedback_summary: (1) S5: Yes treat every mcpServer/elicitation/request as MCP approval gate (RPC method itself is the discriminator); RELAY through approval handler, not auto-accept; mode==='url' must also route. Risk if invariant changes: a real form with required schema or a url with elicitationId could be wrongly auto-accepted. (2) S2: Best signal is source/provider discriminant on tool/message (tool.source==='codex') OR session metadata.flavor==='codex'; signature does not currently receive metadata. Avoid name-prefix detection because mcp__* can be Claude or Codex, functions.* may grow, Codex* misses future dynamic tools. Fixture IDs codex-* are test-only. Renderer registry insufficient because future Codex tools must render inline. (3) Concrete failure risks: D1/S5 could fail if URL-mode approvals are routed but url/elicitationId are dropped from approval payload; could fail if extractMcpToolName cannot parse and overbroad server:* session approval is granted. D2 could fail if Codex 0.125 event payloads do not match fixture shapes. D3 could fail because live imageView events only carry path; previews need accessible URI; non-image MIME silently degrades. D4 could fail if source detection uses prefixes and leaks Claude mcp__*/future functions.*; fixtures need codex metadata or explicit tool source.
codex_consultation.feedback_incorporated: S5 fix relays through approval handler (not auto-accept) — codex's recommended path. URL-mode is included in the gate. The approval payload already passes mode via ApprovalRequest type, mitigating the URL-context concern at the API layer. S2: Codex's preferred source-discriminant doesn't exist on ToolCall (verified at typesMessage.ts:5-24); session metadata is not threaded through shouldRenderToolContent's signature. Falling back to name-prefix is the runtime-available signal. The CLI sessionProtocolMapper output (verified at sessionProtocolMapper.ts:419,459,511,629,684,726) ALWAYS sets Codex tool names to one of these prefixes, so the prefix list captures all Codex sources from this codebase; regression guard tests cover the four Claude generic tool names that must NOT match. Codex's adversarial flag re: 'mcp__* can be Claude or Codex' is acknowledged: in this app, Claude mcp__* tools are NOT in the Grep/Glob/WebSearch/ToolSearch hidden-on-transcript list, so admitting them inline matches the existing scope-policy intent. Codex's D4 'fixtures need codex metadata' is QA's S7 concern — fixture route already passes metadata=null per fixture file; if QA hits this, future cycle expands ToolCall with a source discriminant. Recorded as a known cross-cycle improvement opportunity, not blocking S4.

recommendations: After S4 user-restart and S7 QA, if D4 fixture-route verification surfaces a metadata=null gap (per codex consult), open a follow-up cycle to add a `source: 'codex' | 'claude'` discriminant to ToolCall and switch shouldRenderToolContent to use it instead of name-prefix.
After S7 D3 verification, if non-image attachment is still surfaced anywhere in the UI (e.g. drag-drop, paste), extend the S6 path-b affordance to those entry points (warning toast).
S5 long-term: add a structured logger field for every mcpServer/elicitation/request shape received so future Codex protocol updates can be diff-detected without log-grep guesswork.
S-BUILD: consider adding a CI check that fails when dist contains `experimentalRawEvents: false` (regression guard for S1).
